Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5 SMT solver, branch "lazy").
The working tree has an uncommitted change: run "git diff" in that directory to see it.
The change refactors LiaStarExtension's lazy refinement loop: previously each refinement
round called sub.engine->assertFormula(notD_i) for each newly discovered cone-disjunct,
accumulating assertions forever in the incremental subsolver. Now the code keeps one
cumulative disjunction sub.covered of all discovered disjuncts (in skolem space) and each
round (only when new disjuncts arrived) does: if (sub.pushed) engine->pop(); engine->push();
engine->assertFormula(sub.covered.notNode()); sub.pushed = true.
The base predicate is asserted once at user level 0 in getSubsolver() before any push.
Rationale: each round's refined formula not(D_1 or ... or D_k) implies the previous round's,
so popping the old one loses nothing, and the subsolver holds exactly 2 live assertions,
keeping per-assertion caches bounded.
Key files: src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.{h,cpp} (see lazyCheckStar, getSubsolver,
lazyHilbert), src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_utils.cpp (getDisjunct does checkSat+getValue),
src/smt/solver_engine.{h,cpp} (push/pop semantics).

Lens: lifecycle and edge cases. Read the diff and the whole liastar_extension.{h,cpp}. Look for:
- First round (no disjuncts yet): checkSat on base alone -- consistent with old behavior?
- Round where getDisjunct returns false (complete): literal marked processed; any dangling
  pushed frame problem at destruction (~LiaStarExtension, SolverEngine destructor with
  unpopped user levels)?
- Exceptions: if assertFormula or push throws mid-sequence, is state (sub.pushed flag)
  consistent?
- Could sub.covered grow as a deeply left-nested OR and hit any recursion limit in
  substitution/rewriting/preprocessing?
- Proof mode (d_proofGen) and the trace channels: anything in the new path that breaks them?
Report only real problems introduced by the new code, as findings.

39	
40	namespace liastar {
41	
42	/** Arbitrary-precision integers (the integer type handed to Normaliz). */
43	typedef mpz_class Integer;
44	/** A row of arithmetic terms, e.g. the monomials of one cone contribution. */
45	typedef std::vector<Node> Vector;
46	
47	/**
48	 * Extension to TheoryArith deciding the lia* operator STAR_CONTAINS.
49	 *
50	 * A literal
51	 *     (int.star-contains (lambda ((x_1 Int) ... (x_n Int)) p) v_1 ... v_n)
52	 * asserts that the vector v = (v_1, ..., v_n) belongs to the additive closure
53	 * (the *star*) of the set S = { x in Z^n : p(x), x >= 0 }, i.e. that v is a
54	 * finite sum of vectors each satisfying p. The extension decides such literals
55	 * by reducing them to plain linear integer arithmetic, following
56	 *
57	 * - Levatich, M., Bjorner, N., Piskac, R., Shoham, S. (2020).
58	 *   Solving LIA* Using Approximations.
59	 *   VMCAI 2020.
60	 *   https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-39322-9_17
61	 *
62	 * The reduction views each convex cell (DNF disjunct) of p as a polyhedral
63	 * cone, computes the cone's Hilbert basis and module generators with Normaliz,
64	 * and encodes the star of the union of cells as a system of linear constraints
65	 * over fresh non-negative multipliers (the "star constraints"). The reduction
66	 * lemma `literal = star` is sent through TheoryArith's inference manager. See
67	 * the file comment of liastar_extension.cpp for the full picture.
68	 *
69	 * The main entry point is checkFullEffort(...), called by TheoryArith at
70	 * full/last-call effort with the current candidate arithmetic model. Two
71	 * strategies are available (option arith-lia-star-lazy):
72	 * - eager (`eagerCheckStar`): normalize p to DNF and reduce in one shot;
73	 * - lazy (`lazyCheckStar`): discover one convex cell per refinement round from
74	 *   models of a persistent incremental subsolver, asserting guarded
75	 *   under-approximations until every cell is covered.
76	 */
77	class LiaStarExtension : EnvObj
78	{
79	 public:
80	  LiaStarExtension(Env& env, TheoryArith& containing);
81	  ~LiaStarExtension();
82	
83	  /**
84	   * Does non-context dependent setup for a node connected to a theory:
85	   * registers STAR_CONTAINS terms with the extended theory and records that
86	   * this extension has work to do.
87	   */
88	  void preRegisterTerm(TNode n);
89	
90	  /**
91	   * Performs the main checks for liastar arithmetic, based on the current
92	   * (linear) arithmetic model from `arithModel`. This method may already send
93	   * lemmas, but most lemmas are buffered and sent at LAST_CALL effort by
94	   * TheoryArith. The motivation for this strategy is to allow other
95	   * non-terminating theories (e.g. quantifiers, strings) to run full effort
96	   * checks, before sending the lemmas generated by liastar.
97	   *
98	   * For each STAR_CONTAINS assertion this emits a non-negativity lemma and a
99	   * split on the substituted predicate p[v], and then -- unless the current
100	   * model already satisfies the literal -- reduces the literal via the eager
101	   * or lazy strategy.
102	   *
103	   * @param arithModel a map of the form { v1 -> c1, ..., vn -> cn } which
104	   *   represents the linear arithmetic theory solver's contribution to the
105	   *   current candidate model, where v1, ..., vn are arithmetic variables and
106	   *   c1, ..., cn are constants
107	   * @param termSet the set of terms relevant in the current check
108	   */
109	  void checkFullEffort(std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel,
110	                       const std::set<Node>& termSet);
111	
112	  /** Does this class need a call to check(...) at last call effort? */
113	  bool hasLiaStarTerms() const { return d_hasLiaStarTerms; }
114	
115	 private:
116	  /**
117	   * Collect from TheoryArith's fact queue the STAR_CONTAINS atoms asserted in
118	   * the current context. Both polarities are reduced to the positive atom:
119	   * the reduction lemma `atom = star` handles either polarity (the
120	   * surrounding SAT solver applies the negation).
121	   */
122	  void getAssertions(std::vector<Node>& assertions);
123	
124	  /**
125	   * Normalize the body p of the lambda `n` into DNF and render each disjunct
126	   * as a Normaliz constraint matrix (see `LiaStarUtils::getMatrices`).
127	   *
128	   * @param n a lambda (lambda ((x_1 Int) ... (x_n Int)) p) with p in QF_LIA
129	   * @return one (constraint rows, disjunct node) pair per DNF disjunct of p,
130	   *   i.e. one per cone
131	   */
132	  const std::vector<std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>>
133	  convertQFLIAToMatrices(Node n);
134	
135	  /**
136	   * Eager path: build a Normaliz cone for every DNF disjunct of the predicate
137	   * and accumulate the star constraints over all of them. Empty (infeasible)
138	   * cones are skipped.
139	   *
140	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal; its children after the lambda are the
141	   *   vector v
142	   * @param pairs one (constraint rows, disjunct node) pair per disjunct, as
143	   *   returned by `convertQFLIAToMatrices`
144	   * @return the non-empty cones, each paired with the disjunct it came from
145	   *   (used by `getMembershipDisjuncts` for the debug trace), and the star
146	   *   constraints: fresh multiplier skolems with their side constraints plus
147	   *   the sum constraints tying v to the cones' contributions. Their
148	   *   conjunction is equivalent to `v in S*`.
149	   */
150	  std::pair<std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>,
151	            std::vector<Node>>
152	  getCones(Node n,
153	           const std::vector<std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>>& pairs);
154	
155	  /**
156	   * Lazy path: build the cone for a single disjunct and append it to the list
157	   * of cones for `n[0]` (the lambda) stored in `d_lazyCones`. If the cone is
158	   * empty (the disjunct is infeasible) it is not added.
159	   *
160	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal
161	   * @param pair the disjunct's constraint rows and node, as returned by
162	   *   `LiaStarUtils::getMatrix`
163	   */
164	  void addCone(Node n, const std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>& pair);
165	
166	  /**
167	   * Lazy path: return the star constraints over all cones accumulated so far
168	   * in `d_lazyCones[n[0]]` (the cones added by previous calls to `addCone`).
169	   *
170	   * The per-cone constraints (and their fresh skolems) are computed only for
171	   * cones that have not been processed in a previous call and are accumulated
172	   * in `d_starConstraints[n[0]]`, so the skolems stay stable across refinement
173	   * rounds; the sum constraints, which span all cones, are rebuilt from the
174	   * accumulated `d_lambdas[n[0]]` on each call.
175	   */
176	  std::vector<Node> getStarConstraints(Node n);
177	
178	  /**
179	   * Debug helper, used only for the "liastar-ext-smt" trace. Builds the
180	   * *membership* encoding `v in S`: one existentially quantified formula per
181	   * (cone, module generator) stating that v is the single element
182	   * `g + sum_j l_j h_j` of that cone. The disjunction of all returned
183	   * formulas is equivalent to the predicate itself, which the emitted trace
184	   * queries let an external solver verify.
185	   *
186	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal
187	   * @param cones the cones with their originating disjuncts, as returned by
188	   *   `getCones`
189	   * @return each membership formula paired with the disjunct it encodes
190	   */
191	  std::vector<std::pair<Node, Node>> getMembershipDisjuncts(
192	      Node n, std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>& cones);
193	
194	  /**
195	   * Performs the eager Hilbert-basis reduction for a single STAR_CONTAINS
196	   * literal. Generates the star reduction lemma equating `literal` with the
197	   * conjunction of star constraints derived from the cones of `lambda`
198	   * (== literal[0]), and sends it via the inference manager. Does nothing if
199	   * the literal has already been processed.
200	   */
201	  void eagerCheckStar(Node literal, Node lambda);
202	
203	  /**
204	   * Performs one round of the lazy Hilbert-basis reduction for a single
205	   * STAR_CONTAINS literal: refines the literal's subsolver with the negations
206	   * of the cone-disjuncts discovered since the previous round, then delegates
207	   * to `lazyHilbert`. Does nothing if the literal has been fully reduced.
208	   */
209	  void lazyCheckStar(Node literal, Node lambda);
210	
211	  /**
212	   * A persistent, incremental subsolver dedicated to one lambda (one
213	   * STAR_CONTAINS predicate). It is used to enumerate the convex cells of the
214	   * predicate's satisfying region: it is seeded once with the (nonnegative)
215	   * predicate at the base user level and then refined across rounds. Each
216	   * round's refined formula -- the negated union of every cone-disjunct
217	   * discovered so far -- subsumes (implies) the previous round's, so the
218	   * previous one is popped and the new one asserted in a fresh frame: the
219	   * subsolver always holds exactly the base predicate plus a single refined
220	   * formula, however many rounds have run. This keeps the number of live
221	   * assertions (and the formulas the subsolver caches per assertion) constant
222	   * instead of growing with the number of refinement rounds.
223	   */
224	  struct Subsolver
225	  {
226	    /** the incremental QF_LIA subsolver. */
227	    std::unique_ptr<SolverEngine> engine;
228	    /** the lambda's bound variables ... */
229	    std::vector<Node> from;
230	    /** ... and the fresh skolem constants substituted for them, since a
231	     * subsolver cannot be given a formula with free (bound) variables. */
232	    std::vector<Node> to;
233	    /**
234	     * The (nonnegative) predicate in skolem space. It is already asserted in
235	     * `engine` at the base user level (so it survives every pop); it is kept
236	     * only to read off the predicate's atoms when building a disjunct from
237	     * the model.
238	     */
239	    Node base;
240	    /**
241	     * The union (disjunction), in skolem space, of the cone-disjuncts
242	     * discovered so far. Its negation is the refined formula currently
243	     * asserted in `engine`.
244	     */
245	    Node covered;
246	    /** Whether a refined formula is currently asserted, i.e. whether `engine`
247	     * has a pushed frame to pop before asserting the next refined formula. */
248	    bool pushed = false;
249	    /** number of cones in `d_lazyCones[lambda]` already folded into
250	     * `covered`. */
251	    size_t negated = 0;
252	  };
253	
254	  /**
255	   * Returns the subsolver for `lambda`, creating and seeding it (with the
256	   * nonnegative predicate) on first use.
257	   */
258	  Subsolver& getSubsolver(Node lambda);
259	
260	  /**
261	   * One lazy refinement round for `literal`: ask the subsolver for a model in
262	   * a region of the predicate not yet covered by a cone, read off the convex
263	   * cell containing it (`LiaStarUtils::getDisjunct`), turn the cell into a
264	   * cone, and emit the reduction lemma -- guarded by a fresh boolean while the
265	   * star is still an under-approximation, unconditional once the subsolver
266	   * reports that every cell is covered.
267	   */
268	  void lazyHilbert(Node literal, Subsolver& sub);
269	
270	  /** node manager */
271	  NodeManager* d_nm;
272	  /** commonly used terms */
273	  Node d_true;
274	  Node d_false;
275	  Node d_zero;
276	  Node d_one;
277	  /** The theory of arithmetic containing this extension. */
278	  TheoryArith& d_arith;
279	  /** A reference to the arithmetic state object. */
280	  TheoryState& d_astate;
281	  /** The inference manager of TheoryArith, used to send lemmas. */
282	  InferenceManager& d_im;
283	  /**
284	   * The number of times the main check method (checkFullEffort) has been
285	   * called. Currently only incremented; intended for interleaving strategies.
286	   */
287	  unsigned d_checkCounter;
288	  /** Callback for the extended theory below. */
289	  ExtTheoryCallback d_extTheoryCb;
290	  /** Extended theory, responsible for context-dependent simplification. */
291	  ExtTheory d_extTheory;
292	  /** Do we have any liaStar terms? */
293	  context::CDO<bool> d_hasLiaStarTerms;
294	  /**
295	   * The STAR_CONTAINS literals already fully reduced: eagerly reduced
296	   * literals, and lazily reduced literals whose cone coverage is complete. No
297	   * further lemmas are generated for these.
298	   */
299	  std::vector<Node> d_processedStarTerms;
300	
301	  /**
302	   * The cones accumulated so far during the lazy Hilbert-basis reduction,
303	   * keyed by lambda. Each call to `addCone` appends the cone for the current
304	   * disjunct, and `getStarConstraints` computes the starLia constraints for
305	   * the newly added cones, accumulating them across calls.
306	   */
307	  std::map<Node, std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>>
308	      d_lazyCones;
309	
310	  /**
311	   * The per-cone starLia constraints computed so far for each lambda node
312	   * (`n[0]`). `getStarConstraints` only generates the skolems and constraints
313	   * for cones in `d_lazyCones` that have not been processed yet, appending
314	   * them here, so previously computed constraints (and their skolems) are
315	   * reused across refinement rounds. These are the constraints that are
316	   * independent of the other cones (the (>= mu 0), (>= l 0), and
317	   * (=> (= mu 0) (= l 0)) constraints); the sum constraints span all cones
318	   * and are rebuilt each call.
319	   */
320	  std::map<Node, std::vector<Node>> d_starConstraints;
321	  /**
322	   * The (point, rays) contributions computed so far for each lambda node,
323	   * kept in step with `d_starConstraints`. They are used to rebuild the sum
324	   * constraints over all cones on each call to `getStarConstraints`.
325	   */
326	  std::map<Node, std::vector<std::pair<Vector, std::vector<Vector>>>> d_lambdas;
327	  /** The number of cones in `d_lazyCones[n[0]]` already processed. */
328	  std::map<Node, size_t> d_processedCones;
329	
330	  /**
331	   * The last starLia under-approximation (`star`) computed for each
332	   * STAR_CONTAINS literal by `lazyHilbert`. The model-value check in
333	   * `checkFullEffort` uses it to skip refinement when the current model
334	   * already satisfies the predicate or this under-approximation.
335	   */
336	  std::map<Node, Node> d_lastStarLia;
337	
338	  /**
339	   * The fresh boolean guard of the last (still active) tentative reduction
340	   * `g => (literal = star)` emitted for each STAR_CONTAINS literal by
341	   * `lazyHilbert`. When a later round produces a larger under-approximation,
342	   * the previous guard is deactivated (we assert `(not g)`), so at most one
343	   * tentative reduction is active per literal.
344	   */
345	  std::map<Node, Node> d_lastGuard;
346	
347	  /**
348	   * Lazy proof generator for the lia* lemmas (split, non-negativity, and
349	   * STAR_CONTAINS reduction). Allocated only when proofs are enabled.
350	   */
351	  std::unique_ptr<LiaStarProofGenerator> d_proofGen;
352	
353	  /**
354	   * The incremental subsolver for each lambda (STAR_CONTAINS predicate). Each
355	   * is created lazily and persists for the lifetime of the extension, so the
356	   * predicate's cells are enumerated incrementally across refinement rounds.
357	   */
358	  std::map<Node, Subsolver> d_subsolvers;
359	}; /* class LiaStarExtension */
360	
361	}  // namespace liastar
362	}  // namespace arith
363	}  // namespace theory
364	}  // namespace cvc5::internal
365	
366	#endif /* CVC5__THEORY__ARITH__LIASTAR_EXTENSION_H */
367	
368	#endif /* CVC5_USE_NORMALIZ */

findings.title: Subsolver bookkeeping committed before pop/push/assert leaves inconsistent state if an engine call throws
findings.detail: In lazyCheckStar (lines 537-559), the new code commits sub.covered (lines 547-549) and sub.negated (line 551) BEFORE the engine sequence pop()/push()/assertFormula(), while sub.pushed is only set after assertFormula succeeds (line 558). The old code set sub.negated only after all assertFormula calls, so a throw merely caused benign re-assertion on retry. With the new ordering, if any of the three engine calls throws and the embedding catches the exception and continues solving (incremental API usage; LiaStarExtension and its d_subsolvers persist across check-sats inside TheoryArith), the Subsolver is left permanently inconsistent in one of these ways: (a) pop() succeeds but push() throws: sub.pushed stays true with zero user frames, so the next refinement round's sub.engine->pop() raises ModalException "Cannot pop beyond the first user frame" (src/smt/context_manager.cpp:111) -- note ContextManager::userPop also flips SmtMode via d_state.notifyUserPush() before performing that check, so even the failed pop mutates state; (b) push() succeeds but assertFormula throws on the first refinement (sub.pushed still false): the next round pushes again without popping, permanently leaking an empty user frame; (c) in every throw case, sub.negated has already advanced past the unasserted disjuncts, so until a new disjunct arrives the block at line 537 is skipped and lazyHilbert's checkSat runs WITHOUT the newest refinement, letting getDisjunct rediscover an already-covered cell -- addCone then appends a duplicate cone to d_lazyCones and getStarConstraints mints a duplicate set of star skolems and constraints (bloat and wasted rounds, though not unsoundness, and it self-heals once the duplicate forces the block to re-run). Mitigating factors keeping this minor: the subsolver has its own Options/Env/ResourceManager (no resource-limit or interrupt exceptions propagate into it), so an exception in pop/push/assertFormula essentially indicates an internal error, and in the common embedding the exception propagates out of checkFullEffort and aborts the query anyway. A simple hardening is to perform pop() (setting sub.pushed=false immediately), then push()+assertFormula, and only then advance sub.negated / set sub.pushed=true (folding into a local Node first, assigning sub.covered last).
